title: The Humans - Hampstead Theatre - review
transcript: the humans rig must incur am director by Joe Mantello which I saw at Hampstead Theatre I love a family drama and this one won four Tony Awards when it was on Broadway and it's now been imported with the original production and cast as a portrayal of middle-class family it's spot on true parents leap for Thanksgiving at their daughters new apartment in New York also in attendance at her daughter's partner sister and grandmother the ensemble acting is fantastic they're absolutely believable as a bickering but loving family but this play is about the fears that engulfed so many of today's middle-class families fear of failure unemployment poverty loss of love illness dementia death you can see the weight of these fears physically on all the actors shoulders their most manifesting the father magnificently portrayed by Reed Bernie and the leader a big revelation in the end the set designer David Xin is realistic at naturalistic two-floor gloomy apartment in New York which the couple of only just moved in and the furnitures yet to arrive so although it's their home it has a temporary unholy feel like they could be gone tomorrow and it's spooky there are frightening noises from above and lights going out that suggest darkness could descend at any moment all of which seems to say that while the causes of the theater may have names recession globalization technical revolution aging and so on these are forces as mysterious and uncontrollable as the gods and ghosts that our ancestors believed in I found the plate petered out a little at the end but I give it four stars you
